title: Mainly dry weather expected in parts of the island today
byline: Showers or thundershowers may occur at several places in Western, Sabaragamuwa and Southern provinces and in Nuwara-Eliya district after 1.00 pm, today (22), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Trump threatens to ‘obliterate’ Iran power plants unless Hormuz opens
byline: US President Donald Trump on Saturday (Mar 21) gave Iran a 48-hour deadline to open the Strait of Hormuz to shipping traffic or face the destruction of its energy infrastructure.

title: 90% of private buses withdrawn from service today amid fuel price hike
byline: Around 90% of private buses are expected to be withdrawn from service today (22), according to the Lanka Private Bus Owners’ Association (LPBOA).

title: Over 100 injured in Arad, Dimona in Iranian strikes; Netanyahu vows to attack Tehran on all fronts
byline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday held talks with the Mayor of Arad, Yair Maayan and conveyed his prayers for those injured.

title: Three-wheeler taxi drivers seek fare increase for first km amid rising fuel costs
byline: The National Joint Three-Wheeler Drivers and Industrial Workers’ Association (NJTWDIWA) has formally requested the government to approve a Rs. 20 increase in the fare for the first kilometre of travel, citing the recent rise in petrol prices.

title: Thousands evacuated as Hawaii faces worst flooding in 20 years
byline: Hawaii remains under a statewide flood watch after a severe storm hit the state and prompted officials to order evacuations.

title: Police reveals key details on abduction of woman in Batticaloa; 3 including woman arrested
byline: Police have uncovered key details regarding the incident in the Nellikkadu area of Batticaloa, where an abducted woman was rescued from an abandoned well and the remains of another woman was discovered at the same location.

title: Iran hits Israeli town housing nuclear facility in retaliation for Natanz strike
byline: An Iranian missile has hit the Israeli town of Dimona, home to a nuclear facility, in what Iran said was retaliation for strikes on its own nuclear site at Natanz.

title: Iran threatens to target US, Israeli infrastructure if attacked amid Trump’s power plant ultimatum
byline: Iran threatened Sunday to strike all US and Israeli infrastructure across the region if its facilities came under attack, following an ultimatum from US President Donald Trump.

title: Bus fares expected to rise following fuel price hike
byline: The National Transport Commission (NTC) has announced that measures to revise bus fares will be implemented today (22).

title: Sinopec, Lanka IOC increases fuel prices
byline: Following the recent fuel price revision by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), Sinopec has also increased its fuel prices.

title: Sinopec increases prices of Petrol 95 Octane and Super Diesel above CPC rates
byline: Following the recent fuel price revision by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), Sinopec has also increased its fuel prices.

title: Diesel to be used for nighttime power generation amid fuel supply concerns
byline: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa has stated that the final decision regarding a possible electricity tariff increase will be announced on April 01, 2026.

title: BTS’Jungkook and India’s Arijit Singh announce surprise collaboration
byline: Jungkook of BTS has revealed a surprise collaboration with the Bollywood playback sensation Arijit Singh.

title: 4 Sri Lankans injured in Israel trying to video Iranian attack in Dimona
byline: Four Sri Lankan nationals have been hospitalised after sustaining injuries while attempting to videograph the Iranian attack in Dimona, Israel, the Sri Lankan Embassy in Israel confirmed.

title: Man arrested for illegally hoarding nearly 2,200L of diesel in Ambalantota
byline: A suspect has been arrested by the Hungama Police for illegally hoarding approximately 2,200 litres of diesel at a residence in the Mamadala area of Ambalantota.

title: 153 individuals identified for illegal QR code downloads – Minister Nalinda
byline: Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa stated that nearly 6 million registrations have been recorded so far for the QR code system introduced to limit fuel consumption.

title: Govt bears Rs. 20 bln monthly fuel subsidy; 37,000 MT diesel shipment to arrive March 25 – Minister
byline: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa has announced that a vessel carrying 37,000 metric tons of diesel is scheduled to arrive in the country on March 25.

title: CAA launches special inspections ahead of Sinhala and Hindu New Year
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has initiated a special series of inspections and investigations from March 20, ahead of the upcoming Sinhala and Hindu New Year celebrations.

title: Private bus operators warn of strike over delay in fare revision
byline: The Lanka Private Bus Owners’ Association (LPBOA) has announced that it will launch a nationwide strike commencing at 6:00 p.m. today (22) if the scheduled bus fare revision is not officially announced by 5:00 p.m.

title: Ali Sabry on US aircraft request: “I’m proud the President had the courage to do what is right”
byline: Sri Lanka’s former Justice Minister Ali Sabry has lauded the government’s decision to maintain neutrality by declining a US request to allow aircraft to land at Sri Lankan airports in early March.

title: Qatar says 6 found dead after helicopter crash in territorial waters
byline: Qatar’s Interior Ministry said Sunday that six of the seven people reported missing after a helicopter crash in the country’s territorial waters have been found dead.

title: No decision taken to restrict school days due to fuel situation – Minister
byline: Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa stated that the government has not yet taken any decision to restrict school operations in view of current fuel consumption concerns in the country.

title: Container haulage charges to increase by 20%
byline: Import and export container transportation charges will be increased by 20% from midnight today (22) due to the recent fuel price hike, according to the Container Transport Owners’ Association.

title: Vehicle parking fee collection in Colombo to resume tomorrow – CMC
byline: The Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) has decided to resume the collection of vehicle parking fees across its jurisdiction starting tomorrow (23).

title: Iran is charging $2m from ships passing through Strait of Hormuz - Iranian MP
byline: Iranian Member of Parliament Alaeddin Boroujrrdi has claimed on state TV today that some of the ships that pass through the Strait of Hormuz are being charged ‘‘with a $2 (£1.5) million fee’’ by Iran.

title: Bus fares likely to go up by over 10%; Cabinet approval sought
byline: An increase of over 10% in bus fares has been assessed following the increase in fuel prices and a proposal on the same will be submitted for Cabinet approval tomorrow (23), according to the National Transport Commission (NTC).

title: Modi becomes longest-serving head of govt in India with 8,931 days in office
byline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday created history by becoming the longest-serving head of a government in India, surpassing former Sikkim Chief Minister Pawan Kumar Chamling.

title: Iran threatens to ‘destroy’ energy sites across Middle East if Trump sticks to 48-hour Hormuz ultimatum
byline: Iran has warned global oil prices will stay high for the long term if its key energy infrastructure is attacked.

title: Postal Dept. limits mail transport to alternate days amid fuel crisis
byline: The Department of Posts has decided to limit mail transportation to an alternate-day basis in response to the fuel crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

title: LIOC also hikes prices of Petrol 95 Octane and Super Diesel
byline: Lanka IOC PLC (LIOC) has announced an increase in the prices of several fuel categories, effective from today (22).

title: Fuel price hike severely impacts agricultural sector, warns farmers
byline: Farmers’ associations have stated that the recent increase in fuel prices has had a severe impact on the agricultural sector.

title: Strait of Hormuz will be ‘closed’ if power plants targeted: IRGC
byline: In a statement broadcast by Iranian media, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says it will “completely close” the Strait of Hormuz if the US targets Iranian energy infrastructure.
